entries.title: SEC notice acknowledging North American Derivatives Exchange's registration as a national securities exchange publishes in the Federal Register
entries.facts: The Securities and Exchange Commission published a notice in the Federal Register on September 21, 2026, document number 2026-19215, titled "Acknowledgement of Receipt of Notice of Registration as a National Securities Exchange Pursuant to Section 6(g) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 by North American Derivatives Exchange, Inc." The notice carries Release No. 34-106396 and File No. 10-255 and was filed with the Office of the Federal Register on September 18, 2026. The underlying release, issued September 16, 2026, states that North American Derivatives Exchange, Inc. filed a Form 1-N with the Commission on September 14, 2026, and that "Pursuant to Section 6(g)(3) of the Exchange Act, the Commission hereby acknowledges receipt of the Form 1-N submitted by Nadex." The release states that under Section 6(g)(2)(B) of the Exchange Act "an exchange's registration as a national securities exchange becomes effective contemporaneously with the submission of the written notice on Form 1-N," and that the registration is for the sole purpose of trading security futures products or futures on exempted securities or groups or indexes of securities or options thereon. The Form 1-N as filed gives the name of the exchange as North American Derivatives Exchange, Inc., d/b/a Crypto.com | Derivatives North America, states its state of formation as Delaware, and contains rulebook references to a CFTC-regulated business operating under the brands Crypto.com | Derivatives North America and OG.com. The Federal Register record for the notice contains no DATES section and no comment period.

entries.title: Federal Reserve Board announces three consent prohibition orders, including one involving a former American Express Travel Related Services employee
entries.facts: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System announced on September 18, 2026 the execution of three enforcement actions, each a consent prohibition order barring an individual from further participation in the banking industry. The orders were entered with a former employee of Northstar Bank, Bad Axe, Michigan, for misappropriation of customer funds; a former employee of American Express Travel Related Services Company, Inc., New York, New York, for misapplication of funds and conflicts of interest; and a former employee of Regions Bank, Birmingham, Alabama, for check fraud. The release identifies the three institutions only as former employers; none is named as a respondent, and the release states no monetary penalty against any institution.
entries.source_label: Federal Reserve Board — Enforcement Actions press release, September 18, 2026
entries.relevant_to: card issuers, payment processors, bank-partnered fintechs
